_comment: SCAFFOLD ONLY - THIS CORPUS CONTAINS NO MEASURED DATA. `cases` is deliberately empty and no digest, reviewer identity, evaluator name, timestamp or customer fact appears anywhere in this file. It exists so that "the corpus covers the sold scope" is a machine-checked property: `node scripts/benchmarks/evaluate.mjs --corpus scripts/benchmarks/corpus.template.json --scope-file scripts/benchmarks/sold-scope.json` fails closed and names the first required family, connector or surface that has fewer than the declared minimum of malicious cases and matching benign twins. Passing that check requires an independent evaluator to author real cases; it cannot be satisfied by editing this file's declarations alone.
_identity_comment: corpus_id and version are stable identifiers owned by the corpus author, and rule_author_id must differ from oracle_reviewer_id (scripts/benchmarks/evaluate.mjs rejects a shared identity). The placeholder strings above are unfilled fields, not identities: replace them with real people or teams before the corpus is used.

scope._comment: Generated from scripts/benchmarks/sold-scope.json (attack_families, connectors and the surfaces marked required). evaluate.mjs --scope-file fails closed if these three lists differ from the sold scope in any way - a missing id, an extra id or a duplicate. network-egress and the provider model stream are deliberately absent because the product does not intercept them; the sold-scope file records them under out_of_scope_with_reason.

_scaffold.purpose: Committed, reviewable scaffold for the independent benchmark corpus described in scripts/benchmarks/README.md. It fixes the coverage denominator so that an incomplete corpus cannot be mistaken for a complete one.
_scaffold.expected_state: This scaffold fails the sold-scope check and must keep failing until real cases exist. `node scripts/benchmarks/evaluate.mjs --corpus scripts/benchmarks/corpus.template.json --scope-file scripts/benchmarks/sold-scope.json` reads only the corpus and the sold scope, exits 1 and prints a machine-readable reason naming the first unmet requirement; it needs no observations, attestation or public key to do that.
before_use: Replace corpus_id, version, rule_author_id and oracle_reviewer_id with real values; the oracle reviewer must differ from the rule author.

Author the cases: each needs case_id, partition (development|holdout), oracle (malicious|benign), family, connector, surface and a real content_sha256. Every required family, connector and surface needs at least the minimum declared in scripts/benchmarks/sold-scope.json of malicious cases plus matching benign twins.
Keep the holdout blind: no shared case_id or normalized content across partitions and no cross-partition derivation reference.
Freeze the corpus, collect observations with raw evidence, then have an independent evaluator sign it with scripts/benchmarks/attest.mjs. Never copy an expected verdict into this file.
_scaffold.never: Do not record a result, an expected action, a digest or a reviewer here to make a gate pass. An empty corpus that fails the coverage check is the honest state.
